transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in today because of something that happened at work. I was on a board call, and someone asked a pretty small, standard question about the facility budget. And... I just snapped at them. I got completely irritated and aggressive out of nowhere. That's just not how I run my company, and it's certainly not how I treat my people. It really bothered me, so I figured I should come talk to someone about it.
Have you recently needed much less sleep than usual while still feeling rested?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm sleeping about the same as I usually do. I definitely don't feel like I have any extra energy or anything.
Have you had other sudden outbursts like this before?

No, I haven't. That's really why it bothered me enough to come in. I mean, sure, I can be firm if a situation calls for it, but I don't just lose my temper over a basic question like that. It's never happened before.
Had you used alcohol or any recreational or nonprescribed drugs shortly before the outburst?
No, no nothing like that. I mean, it was a work call. I hadn't had anything to drink, and I don't use any sort of drugs. I was completely sober.
Had there been a significant stressful event or change in your life before this outburst?

Yeah, there was. About six days ago, I was doing a walkthrough at a site and... well, there was an explosion and a fire. This whole thing, me acting like this, has been going on for about six days, ever since that happened.
Since the explosion and fire, have you had unwanted memories of the event that keep coming back?

Yeah, I have. I'll be right in the middle of a call, or... or just sitting there looking at some numbers, and suddenly the blast and that fire by the loading area just jump back into my head. It's like a bad film I didn't ask to see, but it just plays anyway.
Since the explosion, have you felt detached from yourself or as though the world around you is unreal?

Yeah, I have. Sometimes when I'm taking calls from home, the room just looks... distant. And my own voice sounds strange to me. It's almost like I'm watching myself talk instead of being fully there. It's an odd feeling.
Since the explosion, have you been deliberately avoiding thoughts, feelings, places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. I've been keeping away from the new building completely. And... well, even the paperwork. The mortgage folder and the safety reports are just sitting there unopened. The minute I even reach for them, my stomach just drops. So, yeah, I just leave them be.
Since the explosion, have you felt unusually on edge or watchful for danger?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm constantly looking over my shoulder or waiting for something bad to happen. I'm just trying to get through the day, you know? I haven't really noticed being more jumpy or anything like that.
Since the explosion, have you been more easily startled than usual?
Yeah, I have. If a door shuts hard, or... well, even if the printer just kicks on behind me, I jump like something went off again. It takes me a few minutes to get my hands steady after that happens.
Since the explosion, have you had trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

No, my sleep has been about the same as usual. I haven't really had any trouble drifting off or waking up in the middle of the night. Once I'm in bed, I pretty much just sleep straight through till morning.
Since the explosion, have you been unable to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, or affection?

Yeah, I'd say so. Things that usually settle me down—like working on a chess problem, looking over my hiking notes, or even just having dinner with my wife—they all just feel flat right now. I know I should enjoy them, but... I just can't seem to get there.
